question: By what means does the speaker claim to have come to know the determination of the Kaula tradition?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of the Kaulas.
The speaker claims to be known or to have come to know.
This knowledge is attributed to the grace of the one addressed.
inference: The determination of the Kaula tradition is known to the speaker solely by the grace of the lord of the Kaulas.
uncertainties: It is not clear from this verse whether 'jñātaḥ' means 'known' or 'made known'.
plain_english: By your grace, O lord of the Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of the Kaula tradition.
